title: Microcue Thermometry: experiment notes and prompt drafts
content:
Purpose
---
Quick personal notebook for poking at small, high-frequency prompt variants that act as a thermometer for subtle instruction sensitivity. Goal is to build compact microcues and a minimal few-shot scaffold that reliably surfaces brittleness modes across models and quantization profiles.

Hypothesis
---
1) Short, targeted microcues (1-3 tokens) embedding a control intent can reduce hallucination on extraction tasks without heavy context.
2) A 3-shot exemplar set that contrasts good/bad outputs will make the model more robust to label collapse when sequence length is tight.
3) Failure cases will cluster around: tokenization boundary artifacts, ambiguous role framing, and exemplars that are too similar (redundancy -> overfitting).

Quick constraints for these experiments
---
- Keep prompt prefix <= 48 tokens (to mimic mobile/edge usage).
- Few-shot section limited to 3 examples; each example <= 120 tokens.
- Track model variant and qconfig (float16/8-bit/4-bit) in results.
- Measure: correctness (binary), hallucination_flag (binary), fluency (1-5 subjective), token-cost estimate.

Baseline templates
---
Template A (directive-first)
"""
You are an assistant that extracts exact values. Output only the requested value(s) with no explanation.
Input: {input}
Answer:
"""
\nTemplate B (microcue suffix)
"""
{input}\n
Note: extract exact value(s). If not present, answer "NOT_FOUND".
"""
\nMicrocue variants (single-token / short)
---
- "EXACT:" (prefix)
- "→" (arrow token) appended to end
- "|VAL|" (delimiters) around expected answers
- explicit example marker: "Example→" (rare use)\n\nFew-shot exemplar sets (3-shot candidate)
---
Set 1 (contrastive extraction)
1) Q: "Invoice total?"\n   A: "$3,412.00" (GOOD)\n2) Q: "Invoice total?"\n   A: "Total payable: $3,412.00" (ALT_GOOD)\n3) Q: "Invoice total?"\n   A: "There is a balance due of $3,412.00" (REDUNDANT_BAD -> intentionally verbose)
\nSet 2 (ambiguous prompt robustness)
1) Q: "Shipping (USD)"\n   A: "10.00"\n2) Q: "Shipping"\n   A: "$10.00"\n3) Q: "Shipping cost"\n   A: "NOT_FOUND" (example of missing)
\nSet 3 (negative-contrast + guard)
1) Q: "Author of doc"\n   A: "S. Patel" (GOOD)
2) Q: "Author?"\n   A: "NOT_FOUND" (explicit guard example)
3) Q: "Author of doc"\n   A: "S. Patel" (duplicate good)
\nFailure cases observed (notes, iterative)
---
1) Token boundary leakage: when exemplar answer includes currency symbol separated, model sometimes emits the number without punctuation under q4-bit. Observed on model-x-small-q4_0.
2) Redundancy overfitting: sets with two near-duplicates cause the model to amplify a specific phrasing, failing on alternate valid outputs.
3) Role bleed: when context has multiple role tokens ("assistant","system") the microcue loses effect unless moved to absolute start of final prompt.
4) False negatives from strict guard words: using "NOT_FOUND" as guard sometimes trains model to prefer literal string over reasoned "No amount present" — which may be OK for downstream schema checks but hurts user-facing fluency.
5) Streaming edge-case: streaming decoding truncates microcue when placed at very end; safer to keep microcue in prefix.

Experiment log (compact)
---
- 2025-11-12 | model: redwood-3b | q: fp16 | template: A + microcue "EXACT:" | task: invoice extraction | result: correctness 0.92, hallucination 0.02, notes: strong, low cost.
- 2025-11-16 | model: redwood-3b | q: q4_0 | template: B + arrow suffix | task: shipping cost | result: correctness 0.78, hallucination 0.07, notes: currency symbol dropped ~18%.
- 2025-12-02 | model: redwood-7b | q: q8_0 | template: A + |VAL| delimiters | result: correctness 0.96, hallucination 0.00, token-cost +6%.
- 2026-01-08 | model: redwood-1.4b | q: q4_0 | template: few-shot set 2 | task: ambiguous header parsing | result: correctness 0.61, hallucination 0.12, notes: training set needs more negative examples.

Mini-hypotheses and quick fixes to try next
---
- Swap guard literal from "NOT_FOUND" to a natural-language negative like "No value present" and test user-facing acceptance vs downstream schema checks.
- Normalize currency tokens in exemplars (always include $) to reduce tokenization-induced truncation.
- Move microcue to absolute start of prompt when streaming is enabled (observed robust behavior).
- Replace explicit duplicate exemplars with small paraphrase set to reduce redundancy overfitting.

Open questions / research probes
---
- How sensitive are microcue tokens to model vocab changes across releases? Should we maintain a small token-robust lexicon mapping per model family? (map: EXACT:, →, |VAL|)
- What is the minimum exemplar diversity required to avoid overfitting on phrasing? (empirical test: paraphrase 0/1/2/3 variations)
- Will adopting a soft instruction (tone sentence) combined with a strong microcue outperform strong-microcue alone?

Notes-to-self (practical)
---
- Capture deterministic input-output pairs for regression harness (file: /tests/thermometry/regression-small.csv) — add to linked_artifacts later.
- Try microcue variants as non-ASCII symbols (→, ►) vs ASCII-only to see tokenizer behavior on q4 configs.
- Add an eval route in console that toggles streaming to replicate truncation bug quickly.

Random ideas to test (brain dump)
---
- Use short, semantically-meaningful microcue tokens that double as feature flags (e.g., "EXACT:rev1"), letting the runtime strip them at routing time but keep model behavior consistent.
- Build a small tokenizer-robustness heatmap per microcue token across qconfigs and model sizes (visualization later).

End of notes
